about: The ancient dragons who serve the King of Dragons (order 95: only three; D-193; order 97, D-198: each the lord of a dominion): Ashgar of the inferno and Rimewing of the water, hand-written, each a full profile, one of a kind in the bestiary. The third, the storm, is Vaskareth, the King's eldest, a legend (data/legends.json): the category lists her sheet (legends) and the bestiary's storm kind points at her. Validated by tools/lint-figures.mjs.

category.name: The Ancient Dragons
category.note: Only three ancient dragons live, each lord of a dominion: Vaskareth of the storm, the King's eldest and his regent, far the strongest of the three (her sheet stands among the Legends); Ashgar of the inferno and Rimewing of the water, who keep the King's hall while he sleeps.

figures.name: Ashgar

skills.does: A fire white at its heart, lit only in the King's name.

items.does: A claw of the King's own, shed in the first age. It opens the hall under the Wyrmcrown.

goals.why: to keep the King's hall and hoard until he wakes

grudges.why: the Saint struck the King down on the Saint's Stair
Vaskareth gives the King's word as if it were her own

story: The Ancient Inferno Dragon, lord of the fire under the mountains, and the elder of the two who keep the King's hall under the Wyrmcrown while he sleeps.
The lesser dragons keep out of its sky.
It has gone down into the hall and seen the King. The wound has not closed in sixty years, and Ashgar is afraid.

figures.name: Rimewing

skills.does: A wall of black water stands up around it; arrows and fire die in it.
A flood that comes in an hour, over a whole valley.

items.does: A flask from the tarn under the King's hall; it is never warm, and never runs dry.

goals.why: to keep the Black Tarn over the King's hall still
to keep the lesser dragons to the King's old laws

grudges.why: the White Winter freezes the rivers that are Rimewing's roads

story: The Ancient Water Dragon, lord of the water, the second of the two who keep the King's hall. It lies in the Black Tarn under the stone where the King sleeps, and every river out of the Dragon Mountains is its road.
It knows the elder dragons are counting the years, and that some of them hope the King never wakes.
